workload.note: Author ran --num-prompts 30000 (opt-125m, in 800 / out 75). We run 2000 prompts per repeat so 5 repeats x 4 arms fit in a session; same per-step hot path (compute_slot_mapping runs every step), throughput ratio comparable, absolute tok/s not 1:1 (different GPU, shorter run). Weights come from the HF cache mounted at /root/.cache/huggingface (.weights/hf on the host). Args match the author: vllm 0.10.1 gives >=70 GiB GPUs max_num_seqs=1024/max_num_batched_tokens=16384 by default, we must pass them; 30000 prompts ~16 min/run so repeats=1.

reported.note: author gave a ratio/percentage only; applied to our reproduced baseline

gap.note: Author: `--num-prompts 30000`, 268→274 req/s (+2.07 %, single run, no sd) on an 8-GPU node; ours `--num-prompts 2000`, 30.1→30.2 req/s (+0.2 %, sd 0.7 %). The PR saves ~400 µs of host work per step; it is only visible when the step is host-bound. On the 5070 Ti the same opt-125m step is ~9× slower on the GPU side (26 K vs 235 K tok/s), so the host saving is <0.3 % of step time — consistent with what we measured. Secondary config gap: vLLM 0.10.1 (`vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1633`) defaults `max_num_seqs=1024, max_num_batched_tokens=16384` when the GPU has ≥ 70 GiB (and is not an A100), else `256 / 8192`, so the author's slot-mapping loop ran over 4× more requests and 2× more tokens per step. To match the author's args: add `--max-num-seqs 1024 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384` and `--num-prompts 30000` (≈16 min/run; 1 repeat per arm is enough, the metric is already an average over 30000 requests). Even then expect ≤1 % here. Verdict: hardware; the author's 2 % is below any reasonable noise gate anyway.
